newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSTANT VIEW - NZ jobs data reaffirms easing bias.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - NZ jobs data reaffirms easing bias.

text.p: Following is a list of analysts' reactions to New Zealand March quarter jobs and unemployment data published at 2245 GMT on Tuesday.
The data showed the unemployment rate at rising to 6.4 percent from 5.9 percent and employment growth falling 0.1 percent in the quarter for an annual rise of 1.1 percent.
Expectations were for an unemployment rate of 6.15 percent, quarterly employment growth of 0.35 percent for an annual growth rate of 1.71 percent and a participation rate of 65.77 percent.
"The bonds look great, the New Zealand dollar looks vulnerable and that's the view we've had since the beginning of the year," Plank said.
BANKERS TRUST NZ CHIEF ECONOMIST DAVID PLANK
"It will just reaffirm the easing bias by the Reserve Bank.
"The story remains intact -- that the Reserve Bank is in easing mode. It is probably going to ease in June if the market does not do it for it, and today's number just reinforces that view," he said.
"Maybe this suggests that companies are under pressure, so maybe you are going to get continued earnings disappointments. Company profit numbers are showing that up already.
